title: Audio Content & Transcripts 🎧
description: Provide transcripts for podcasts, audio players with keyboard support, and live audio alternatives.

slides.title: Audio Accessibility: The Basics 🔊
slides.content:
Audio content includes podcasts, interviews, music, and sound effects. For deaf and hard‑of‑hearing users, audio must have a **text alternative**.

* **Transcripts** – a full text version of spoken content and important sound effects.
* **Captions** – synchronized text for audio that is part of a video (covered in next lesson).
* **Audio controls** – must be keyboard accessible.

WCAG requires transcripts for prerecorded audio (Level A) and live audio (if possible).

quizData.question: What is the minimum requirement for a podcast episode on your website to meet WCAG A?
quizData.explanation: For audio-only content, a transcript is required (WCAG 1.2.1).

slides.title: Creating Good Transcripts 📝
slides.content:
A transcript should include:

* All spoken words (verbatim).
* Speaker identification ("Interviewer:", "Dr. Smith:").
* Important sound effects ("[doorbell rings]", "[laughter]").
* Links to mentioned resources.

Place the transcript directly on the page below the audio player or link to a separate page. Make it easy to find.

slides.title: Accessible Audio Players 🎛️
slides.content:
Native `<audio controls>` provides basic accessibility: play/pause, seek, volume are keyboard‑operable.

Custom audio players must:

* Use `<button>` elements for controls (not divs).
* Have accessible labels (e.g., `aria-label='Play'`).
* Support keyboard shortcuts (Space for play/pause, arrow keys for seek/volume).
* Be fully operable without a mouse.

Avoid auto‑playing audio – it interferes with screen readers.

slides.title: Native Audio Player with Transcript
slides.codeSnippet:
View transcript

[Intro music]

Host: Welcome to the show...

quizData.question: What is the best HTML element for a custom play button?
quizData.explanation: A native `<button>` provides built‑in keyboard and role semantics.

slides.title: Live Audio Streams 📻
slides.content: For live audio (e.g., radio streams), provide a note that a transcript will be available later, or offer live captions (using a service). WCAG AAA requires live captions, but at minimum, indicate the lack of alternative.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `<details>` for transcripts
It's a native disclosure widget – accessible, keyboard‑friendly, and requires no JavaScript.
